107	    val postNotificationPermissionLauncher = rememberLauncherForActivityResult(
108	        contract = ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission(),
109	        onResult = { isGranted ->
110	            if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU && !isGranted) {
111	                isPostNotificationPermanentlyDeclined = !shouldShowRational(Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS)

115	    )
116	
117	    fun requestPostNotificationPermissionIfNeeded() {
118	        if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU) return
119	        if (!state.isPermissionGranted) return
120	        val granted = ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(
121	            context,
122	            Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS,
123	        ) == PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
124	        if (!granted) {
125	            postNotificationPermissionLauncher.launch(Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS)

131	            Lifecycle.Event.ON_RESUME -> {

# A visual language for Farhan notifications

Start with two views of the same notification. Inbox should show what happened and retain the original message. Overview should show when Farhan may deliver it and what could hold it back. When six separate posts come from one chat, Inbox can show one conversation and Overview can account for six entries. Those views can share the underlying records without implying that their counts mean the same thing.

## Recommendations

1. Try cards by kind in Inbox, starting with conversations where Farhan has a stable thread ID and a plain row for everything else. Keep the original notification a tap away.
2. Try a delivery timeline in Overview. Mark the next eligible batch and show the current points available. Label a forecast as an estimate and give budget holds a separate state.

## What the owner's research contributes

- **Give each object ways to explain itself.** In Glamorous Toolkit, Phlow discovers inspector views declared on an object's class and its superclasses. Each view can decide whether it applies to the object. One object can expose a list, a tree, a graph, raw text, or a small hand-built view. In Farhan, the same notification can answer “What happened?”, “Why is it waiting?” and “What did the app actually send?” from the same record. The kind chooses the first view. # A visual language for Farhan notifications

Start with two views of the same notification. Inbox should show what happened and retain the original message. Overview should show when Farhan may deliver it and what could hold it back. When six separate posts come from one chat, Inbox can show one conversation and Overview can account for six entries. Those views can share the underlying records without implying that their counts mean the same thing.

Missing action metadata leaves the original content as the way to find out. |
| Repeats | A loop glyph and a count such as “4 repeats in 24 h” belong on a collapsed series. | Require a stable series key or a documented, inspectable grouping rule. Distinguish an update to one post from a new repeat. |
| Next eligible delivery | A local time heads each group on a vertical list. In Overview a shared time scale lets priority lanes show the next tick. Put “Waiting for budget” or “Delivery unavailable” in a labelled group when appropriate. | Recompute when settings or queue state change. Include the date beyond today. The forecast and its reason come from the same snapshot. |

Keep the first line readable with one hand and use the whole row for the main tap. Use a 48 dp target for a disclosure or explicit action. Allow labels to wrap at large font sizes and provide an accessible summary for drawn marks; at narrow widths the timeline can read as a vertical list. Check both Material color schemes and grayscale. Use shape, label, and position as redundant cues. Reserve movement for an optional transition when state changes and keep all meaning visible with reduced motion. Keep message text, sender names, amounts as posted, and event details as text. [Compose accessibility defaults](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/accessibility/api-defaults)

# Farhan layout shift and performance baseline

The measured release-like APK grew 2.69%. The six accepted current debug launches establish a noisy sample. The shared emulator could not provide a matched before/now run, so runtime limits remain a proposal. Use slot-matched skeletons for the first layout fixes.

**Baseline builds.** Before is `3668f5e` and now is `717faf6`. The local `rework` and `main` merge base is `a35331d`. Two intervening commits add Entire.io and fix three-button navigation padding. `3668f5e` adds the Nix shell and specs. Its child `4abfe19` starts the overhaul with classification, batching, database changes, and the notification dashboard. `53c83d9` adds app priorities and scheduling, `62fdbf2` adds delivery budgets, and `6393833` moves bulk catalog assembly off Main. The settings portability and startup changes after that correction are part of the requested now build. End-to-end deltas include all intervening changes.

## What Edge measures

I used `feat/layout-shift` at `5a7260f57` for the original implementation and `cls-pilot` at `06fc8bf5b` for the subsequent appearance and consistency rules. The `cls-spiral` worktree at `b7dc9fd81` is a mock-up branch for the ring, scrub panel, header, and accordions. Its visual tests do not establish a separate scoring policy.

The Flutter widget-test probe turns the painted tree into explicitly timed frames. It tracks string-keyed elements, with opt-in synthetic IDs for unkeyed text, inputs, tappable controls, cards, and progress indicators. A synthetic ID uses the element kind, nearest keyed scope, up to three ancestor types, and a first-seen ordinal retained for the life of the element. Cards omit the ancestor types so a loading box can match the card that fills it. Sibling index and visible text stay out of identity. The probe clips to scroll viewports, drops hidden routes when configured, and avoids double-counting a control and its wrappers or label. Placeholder roles come from skeleton keys, loading widgets, and annotated pending content. Shared slots have explicit `shared:<name>` IDs. The later `PendingContent` implementation keeps the real card and chart boxes, replaces pending values with neutral bars or chart paint, and excludes pending controls from pointer input, focus, and accessibility. It uses a section loading label and has no shimmer.

| Rule | Edge standard policy |
| --- | --- |
| Move, resize, recolor | Match by ID in consecutive frames. Geometry is bounding-union area / viewport area × center distance / longest viewport side. Color uses max RGB difference / 255, weighted by area and 0.5. An unchanged center and color score zero in this term even for a symmetric resize. Role weights are paragraph 2, input 3, control 1.5, media 1, decorative 0.5, other 1, and placeholder 0.5 in the pilot. |
| Interaction timing | Piecewise-linear response multiplier (ms, cost) of (100, 0), (200, 0.1), (300, 0.3), (400, 0.5), (500, 1). Beyond 500 ms or without an interaction, cost is 1. Animation starting within 100 ms earns 100 ms of grace. Qualifying chains start at or after 75 ms, end within 2 s, and have 200–400 ms cycles, multiplying cost by 0.5. |
| Focus and intent | Focus distance is normalized and weighted by recency with a 2 s half-life. The last interaction's declared intent target gets a 0.5 discount with source–target distance weighting. Focused elements get a 2× multiplier. Packed controls within 8 logical px get 3× when they move relative to each other. A visible disabled shield lasting 400–1,000 ms gives a 0.8 multiplier under the policy's focus and timing conditions. |
| Hazard and control movement | In-window latency floors are 0.5 for the source or its packed neighbor, 0.5 for current/recent focus, and 0.3 for packed relative movement. Take the highest applicable floor. A hazardous control also scores at least 0.1 × min(1, center displacement / 48 logical px), with the dense multiplier and disabled discount where applicable. Intent targets skip these floors. This catches a small control moving under a finger even in the free response window. |
| Cover | A new or growing overlap covering at least 25% of a focusable element adds the covered fraction × cover weight 1 × adjusted latency, doubled when focused. The pilot accounts for ancestry and avoids recharging an already present cover. |
| Load | Score the last changed frame before the next interaction or the capture end, including ID appearance and disappearance. Multiply 0.25 by the load curve (100, 0), (400, 0.1), (1,000, 0.3), (2,000, 0.6), (4,000, 1), with animation grace and qualifying-chain discount. A change on the last captured frame costs the full 0.25. |
| Appearance | The initial frame for an interaction is free. Later new IDs pay visible uncovered area / viewport area × role weight × 0.5 × the load curve. The exact union of vanished placeholder intersections offsets the area. At least 90% coverage is free. Swapping one real card for another pays in full. |
| Consistency | Compare settled frames directly. Cross-screen comparisons use shared IDs, revisits use all tracked IDs, and empty-versus-loaded uses card IDs. Up to 1 logical px of center and dimension drift is free. Above tolerance use the clipped geometry/area formula with role weights plus a floor of 0.1 × min(1, max(center drift, size drift) / 8), taking the larger score. Placeholder matches skip the floor. A visible one-sided ID pays its viewport-area fraction. Consistency has no interaction timing discount. |
| Separate launch and motion checks | First paint is capped at 20 ms and the relative luminance of `#222222`. The guard checks native launch colors in light and dark. Pumped tests cannot establish physical first-paint timing. Reduced-motion spans are capped at 150 ms, with a 750–2,000 ms chain-cycle exception. |

Findings are per element, frame, and rule. Standard warning/error thresholds are 0.05/0.25. Strict uses 0.03/0.15 and lenient uses 0.08/0.40, with their own weights and curves. Total sums findings. Edge uses scenario-specific assertions too. The pilot's metric-detail and secondary-screen probes cap total at 0.016 in their respective configurations, and metric detail caps individual findings at 0.002. Home/Health wearable controls have 0.05 total caps in their tests. The consistency tests reject findings at the warning threshold. There is no universal total cap or score-updating ratchet in these checks. Edge's separate shrink-only file/occurrence gates cover legacy guard debt. [Original design and standard policy](/home/mini/Documents/repos/edge.worktrees/cls-pilot/docs/LAYOUT_SHIFT.md) · [Pilot probe](/home/mini/Documents/repos/edge.worktrees/cls-pilot/test/support/layout_shift_probe.dart)

The standard phone probe uses a 390 × 844 logical viewport and fake pump offsets of 0, 16, 50, 100, 200, 300, 500, 1,000, and 2,000 ms. The pilot settles declared height transitions at those checkpoints and scores their endpoints. The heavy probe samples against a monotonic clock at roughly 16 ms with a 750 ms quiet window and 20 s cap.

The suite exercises cold open, loading to ready, stored-data refresh landing, scrolled reload, route push, settings accordion expand, date changes, marked-moment open/choice/Undo/inline input/focused neighbor/Save, shared tab positions, revisit, and first-launch consistency. Heavy SQLite-backed tests are opt-in via `LAYOUT_SHIFT_HEAVY=1`. Normal policy laws, fixtures, screen assertions, and launch guards run as Flutter tests. The checked-in workflow invokes the full suite through `scripts/capture_proof.py` on PRs and pushes to main. Visual goldens and before/after shots are reviewed with the owner before regeneration. They pin appearance at selected frames. The scorer enforces behavior between frames. [Merge notes](/home/mini/Documents/repos/edge.research/cls-merge-notes.md) · [Review merge scope](/home/mini/Documents/repos/edge.research/cls-review-merge-scope.md) · [October 24 plan](/home/mini/Documents/repos/edge.research/cls-plan-2026-10-24.md) · [Pilot workflow](/home/mini/Documents/repos/edge.worktrees/cls-pilot/.github/workflows/test.yml)

Keep tapped controls in place and reserve a status/action slot so feedback and Undo do not reflow them. Long work can use reserved space or unused space. Keep the scroll anchor during a refresh. The owner approved conditional nudge and detected-activity cards as specific exceptions and asked for saved-answer row height to remain stable. ## Compose probe and proposed rules

Keep the scorer in pure Kotlin. Port Edge's data model, standard policy, and formulas, including the late-arrival and consistency rules from the pilot. Use Edge fixtures as cross-language oracles plus hand-calculated cases. Edge keeps a disclosure’s intentionally animated height in its own check. Capture the intermediate Compose frames and record that intent so an unrelated moving sibling still counts. Start with explicitly named slots in the real screen composables. Read `SemanticsNode.boundsInRoot` in the unmerged tree, normalize physical pixels to dp, and clip each element to the screen and its scrolling viewport. A test tag or custom semantics property identifies each card, control, and important text slot. Keep focus, enabled state, placeholder role, ancestry, and the action/intent pair in the frame model. Read declared surface color where needed. Semantics bounds alone cannot sample painted color, tell actual occlusion, or identify skeleton paint that has no semantics. Give the skeleton's outer slot the bounds marker and keep its decorative shapes out of accessibility. For popups and dialogs, capture each Compose root separately or map their host offsets into one coordinate system with an explicit layer order.

Use the existing Android instrumentation setup in `app/src/androidTest` (`UsageOverviewE2E`, Hilt runner and Compose test APIs). Neither pin has a Robolectric dependency or runner. JVM tests cover the pure scorer. An emulator `ComposeTestRule` sets `mainClock.autoAdvance = false`, captures the start frame, releases a test-controlled repository milestone, calls `advanceTimeByFrame()`, synchronizes layout and Android draw, then snapshots the tagged slots. Record clock time and assert that loading and loaded states both occurred. The main clock drives Compose and leaves host rendering, IME, and system-level work on Android's clock. Use separately synchronized device cases for real insets and OS motion. For repeatable unit geometry, hold viewport, navigation mode, font scale, data, and inset inputs fixed. [Compose test synchronization](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/testing/synchronization) · [SemanticsNode bounds](https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/androidx/compose/ui/semantics/SemanticsNode)

For a `LazyColumn`, use the domain key (notification ID, package name, or a named card). Track the first visible key and offset. Measure refresh while scrolled and anchor retained rows across reordering. During an explicit swipe, measure the pinned chrome in root coordinates and rows relative to the intentional list motion. A row entering the viewport due to the swipe is different from content arriving late into a still viewport. Witness the scroll actually happened, and also check the anchors when the fling settles. For skeletons without known entity IDs, keep a stable section slot and named skeleton footprints within it. When real IDs arrive, apply Edge's vanished-placeholder coverage rule to those rows. Avoid binding row identities to positions. Track status and navigation bar insets from the same root and grant the IME animation an explicit action/intent. Measure preserved controls relative to the visible content viewport during that animation and compare settled geometry within the same inset state. Run gesture and three-button navigation separately, including the schedule and priority rank fields with the keyboard open.

**Default fix: a skeleton that reserves the loaded slot.** Keep the outer layout in the screen and share a `SkeletonSlot` for its pending interior. Give loaded and pending content the same width, height constraints, padding, shape, and outer slot ID. Derive dimensions from the row/card contract at the active width and font scale. Skeleton shimmer is optional and off under reduced motion. Use one accessible loading status for the section. Do not give its shapes separate focus targets. In Edge `4542141b`, a spinner is mapped to its sizing wrapper and content text/hash is diagnostic only. For Compose the same stable slot ID, equal bounds, and stable sampled surface color yield zero movement or appearance for a slot fill. If real children have new IDs, the vanished placeholder footprint offsets the appear rule. Score load and any genuine color or neighbor change separately. Pair the zero-shift test with a failing smaller-skeleton case and a late real-card insertion case.

| Screen at `717faf6` | Source evidence and skeleton to try |
| --- | --- |
| Inbox | `NotificationFilterScreen` picks the empty branch when the active or cleared list is empty. Before the first Flow publication that can show **No notifications**. Reserve the list under the existing filter bar with row-shaped skeletons, a fixed app icon box, and the same title/body/time line slots. Use the notification ID on loaded rows. Publish the empty message only after a confirmed empty result. Keep selected filters and date headers anchored during arrivals and dismissals. |
| App priorities | `AppPriorityScreen` shows a centered `CircularProgressIndicator` while loading with no cached apps. Cached rows can then be replaced and reordered after discovery. The pinned screen has fixed action glyphs and no package drawable. Keep the package-keyed row layout and reserve a fixed icon box whenever package icons are added, including rows whose drawable is unavailable. Match collapsed row width, minimum height, and title/action geometry in the skeleton. Keep cached rows visible through discovery. Within an expanded row, reserve known channel and rank sections and test IME inset changes independently. |
| Dashboard | `NotificationDashboardScreen` replaces a spinner-only loading branch with the toolbar and list. Flood, standing alerts, top chatters, and errors are conditional and can move controls below them. Keep the toolbar and persistent summary widgets mounted. Render placeholder data inside the loaded widget shells, with dedicated slots for status text, count, ring, and action. Give alerts a designated slot or append them beyond the stable section. Test whether that section is still visible at a scrolled position when alerts arrive. |
| Usage | `UsageOverviewScreen` gates the summary on loading and non-empty tracked apps, swaps a spinner/empty message/chart branch, and renders app items without explicit keys. Keep the day selector, ring/chart frame, legend, and readout rows mounted. Use an empty ring track of the same diameter and a fixed-width dash for undefined ratios. Map NaN or zero denominators to an unavailable readout before drawing. `UsageBarInfo` formats a ratio using `value / total.toFloat()` without a zero guard at that site. A visible NaN was not measured. Key app rows by package and preserve list position across day and range updates. |

## What Edge measures

I used `feat/layout-shift` at `5a7260f57` for the original implementation and `cls-pilot` at `06fc8bf5b` for the subsequent appearance and consistency rules. The `cls-spiral` worktree at `b7dc9fd81` is a mock-up branch for the ring, scrub panel, header, and accordions. Its visual tests do not establish a separate scoring policy.

The Flutter widget-test probe turns the painted tree into explicitly timed frames. It tracks string-keyed elements, with opt-in synthetic IDs for unkeyed text, inputs, tappable controls, cards, and progress indicators. A synthetic ID uses the element kind, nearest keyed scope, up to three ancestor types, and a first-seen ordinal retained for the life of the element. Cards omit the ancestor types so a loading box can match the card that fills it. Sibling index and visible text stay out of identity. The probe clips to scroll viewports, drops hidden routes when configured, and avoids double-counting a control and its wrappers or label. Placeholder roles come from skeleton keys, loading widgets, and annotated pending content. Shared slots have explicit `shared:<name>` IDs. The later `PendingContent` implementation keeps the real card and chart boxes, replaces pending values with neutral bars or chart paint, and excludes pending controls from pointer input, focus, and accessibility. It uses a section loading label and has no shimmer.

| Rule | Edge standard policy |
| --- | --- |
| Move, resize, recolor | Match by ID in consecutive frames. Geometry is bounding-union area / viewport area × center distance / longest viewport side. Color uses max RGB difference / 255, weighted by area and 0.5. An unchanged center and color score zero in this term even for a symmetric resize. Role weights are paragraph 2, input 3, control 1.5, media 1, decorative 0.5, other 1, and placeholder 0.5 in the pilot. |
| Interaction timing | Piecewise-linear response multiplier (ms, cost) of (100, 0), (200, 0.1), (300, 0.3), (400, 0.5), (500, 1). Beyond 500 ms or without an interaction, cost is 1. Animation starting within 100 ms earns 100 ms of grace. Qualifying chains start at or after 75 ms, end within 2 s, and have 200–400 ms cycles, multiplying cost by 0.5. |
| Focus and intent | Focus distance is normalized and weighted by recency with a 2 s half-life. The last interaction's declared intent target gets a 0.5 discount with source–target distance weighting. Focused elements get a 2× multiplier. Packed controls within 8 logical px get 3× when they move relative to each other. A visible disabled shield lasting 400–1,000 ms gives a 0.8 multiplier under the policy's focus and timing conditions. |
| Hazard and control movement | In-window latency floors are 0.5 for the source or its packed neighbor, 0.5 for current/recent focus, and 0.3 for packed relative movement. Take the highest applicable floor. A hazardous control also scores at least 0.1 × min(1, center displacement / 48 logical px), with the dense multiplier and disabled discount where applicable. Intent targets skip these floors. This catches a small control moving under a finger even in the free response window. |
| Cover | A new or growing overlap covering at least 25% of a focusable element adds the covered fraction × cover weight 1 × adjusted latency, doubled when focused. The pilot accounts for ancestry and avoids recharging an already present cover. |
| Load | Score the last changed frame before the next interaction or the capture end, including ID appearance and disappearance. Multiply 0.25 by the load curve (100, 0), (400, 0.1), (1,000, 0.3), (2,000, 0.6), (4,000, 1), with animation grace and qualifying-chain discount. A change on the last captured frame costs the full 0.25. |
| Appearance | The initial frame for an interaction is free. Later new IDs pay visible uncovered area / viewport area × role weight × 0.5 × the load curve. The exact union of vanished placeholder intersections offsets the area. At least 90% coverage is free. Swapping one real card for another pays in full. |
| Consistency | Compare settled frames directly. Cross-screen comparisons use shared IDs, revisits use all tracked IDs, and empty-versus-loaded uses card IDs. Up to 1 logical px of center and dimension drift is free. Above tolerance use the clipped geometry/area formula with role weights plus a floor of 0.1 × min(1, max(center drift, size drift) / 8), taking the larger score. Placeholder matches skip the floor. A visible one-sided ID pays its viewport-area fraction. Consistency has no interaction timing discount. |
| Separate launch and motion checks | First paint is capped at 20 ms and the relative luminance of `#222222`. The guard checks native launch colors in light and dark. Pumped tests cannot establish physical first-paint timing. Reduced-motion spans are capped at 150 ms, with a 750–2,000 ms chain-cycle exception. |

Findings are per element, frame, and rule. Standard warning/error thresholds are 0.05/0.25. Strict uses 0.03/0.15 and lenient uses 0.08/0.40, with their own weights and curves. Total sums findings. Edge uses scenario-specific assertions too. The pilot's metric-detail and secondary-screen probes cap total at 0.016 in their respective configurations, and metric detail caps individual findings at 0.002. Home/Health wearable controls have 0.05 total caps in their tests. The consistency tests reject findings at the warning threshold. There is no universal total cap or score-updating ratchet in these checks. Edge's separate shrink-only file/occurrence gates cover legacy guard debt. package ly.com.tahaben.notification_filter_presentation.components

import java.text.DateFormat
import java.text.SimpleDateFormat
import java.util.Calendar
import java.util.Date
import java.util.Locale

fun Long.toNotificationDateLabel(nowMillis: Long = System.currentTimeMillis()): String {
    if (this <= 0L) return ""

    val todayCal = Calendar.getInstance().apply {
        timeInMillis = nowMillis
        set(Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY, 0)
        set(Calendar.MINUTE, 0)
        set(Calendar.SECOND, 0)
        set(Calendar.MILLISECOND, 0)
    }
    val todayStart = todayCal.timeInMillis
    val yesterdayStart = todayStart - 86_400_000L

    val weekStartCal = (todayCal.clone() as Calendar).apply {
        firstDayOfWeek = Calendar.SUNDAY
        set(Calendar.DAY_OF_WEEK, Calendar.SUNDAY)
    }
    val weekStart = weekStartCal.timeInMillis

    val date = Date(this)
    return when {
        this >= todayStart -> "Today"
        this >= yesterdayStart -> "Yesterday"
        this >= weekStart -> SimpleDateFormat("EEEE", Locale.getDefault()).format(date)
        else -> SimpleDateFormat("MMMM d", Locale.getDefault()).format(date)
    }
}

fun Long.toNotificationDateTimeLabel(nowMillis: Long = System.currentTimeMillis()): String {
    if (this <= 0L) return ""
    val dateLabel = toNotificationDateLabel(nowMillis)
    val timeLabel = DateFormat.getTimeInstance(DateFormat.SHORT, Locale.getDefault()).format(Date(this))
    return "$dateLabel • $timeLabel"
}

    @ColumnInfo(defaultValue = "0") val isCleared: Boolean = false,

    @ColumnInfo(defaultValue = "''") val sourceSession: String = "",

/** SQL shared with executable SQLite query fixtures. All row results are bounded before domain mapping. */
object NotificationQueries {
    const val INVALIDATE = "UPDATE notificationitementity SET deliveryInvalidated = 1, priorityReason = 'Not proxied after intake overflow. Open the source app.' WHERE sourceSession = :session AND sourceEventOrder > 0 AND sourceEventOrder <= :order AND isDelivered = 0 AND isCleared = 0"
    const val INBOX = """SELECT * FROM notificationitementity WHERE isCleared = :cleared
        AND (:priority IS NULL OR (CASE WHEN isRead = 0 AND priority != 1 AND timestamp < :standingCutoff THEN MIN(priority + 1, 4) ELSE priority END) = :priority)
        AND (:search = '' OR instr(lower(coalesce(title,'') || ' ' || coalesce(text,'') || ' ' || coalesce(appName,'') || ' ' || creatorPackage), lower(:search)) > 0)
        ORDER BY timestamp DESC, id DESC LIMIT :limit OFFSET :offset"""
    const val COUNTS = """SELECT COUNT(*) AS total,
        coalesce(SUM(CASE WHEN timestamp >= :dayStart THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS today,
        coalesce(SUM(CASE WHEN isRead = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS unread,
        coalesce(SUM(CASE WHEN isRead = 0 AND priority != 1 AND timestamp < :standingCutoff THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS standing,
        coalesce(SUM(CASE WHEN timestamp >= :floodStart THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS recent,
        coalesce(SUM(CASE WHEN isRead = 0 AND priority = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS criticalUnread
        FROM notificationitementity WHERE isCleared = 0"""
    const val PRIORITIES = "SELECT priority AS label, COUNT(*) AS count FROM notificationitementity WHERE isCleared = 0 GROUP BY priority"
    const val CATEGORIES = "SELECT category AS label, COUNT(*) AS count FROM notificationitementity WHERE isCleared = 0 GROUP BY category"
    const val CHATTERS = "SELECT creatorPackage AS packageName, coalesce(MAX(appName), creatorPackage) AS appName, COUNT(*) AS count FROM notificationitementity WHERE isCleared = 0 GROUP BY creatorPackage ORDER BY count DESC, creatorPackage ASC LIMIT 5"
    const val BATCHES = """WITH groups AS (SELECT creatorPackage, timestamp / :windowMillis AS bucket, COUNT(*) AS count,
        MIN(priority) AS priority, MAX(timestamp) AS latestTimestamp, MIN(timestamp) AS oldestTimestamp
        FROM notificationitementity WHERE isCleared = 0 GROUP BY creatorPackage, timestamp / :windowMillis
        ORDER BY priority ASC, latestTimestamp DESC, creatorPackage ASC LIMIT :limit)
        SELECT groups.creatorPackage AS packageName, groups.bucket * :windowMillis AS rangeStart,
        (groups.bucket + 1) * :windowMillis AS rangeEnd, groups.count, groups.priority, groups.latestTimestamp, groups.oldestTimestamp,
        latest.appName, latest.category, latest.title, latest.text
        FROM groups JOIN notificationitementity AS latest ON latest.id = (SELECT id FROM notificationitementity AS item
        WHERE item.isCleared = 0 AND item.creatorPackage = groups.creatorPackage AND item.timestamp / :windowMillis = groups.bucket
        ORDER BY item.timestamp DESC, item.id DESC LIMIT 1)
        ORDER BY groups.priority ASC, groups.latestTimestamp DESC, groups.creatorPackage ASC"""
    const val BATCH_ITEMS = """SELECT * FROM notificationitementity WHERE isCleared = 0 AND creatorPackage = :packageName
        AND timestamp >= :start AND timestamp < :end ORDER BY timestamp DESC, id DESC LIMIT :limit OFFSET :offset"""
    const val STANDING = """SELECT * FROM notificationitementity WHERE isCleared = 0 AND isRead = 0 AND priority != 1 AND timestamp < :cutoff
        ORDER BY timestamp ASC, id ASC LIMIT :limit"""
}

I also noticed the in-memory `notificationActions` map in ServiceUtil that holds the action titles. Next I'm working out how to split the Inbox list so sent and unsent items are visually separated.

I'm weighing how to separate sent from waiting items in the Inbox list, with headers and status chips on each card. Since the query sorts by timestamp and pages 100 at a time, partitioning only within each page could put a waiting header on a page of mixed items. Changing the SQL order would fix that but would touch shared test fixtures, so I'm leaning toward partitioning in the ViewModel and leaving the query alone.

I'm now thinking about performance in the list item: precomputing the UI model off the main thread, and making the per-item composable cheaper, since the menu options lambdas are rebuilt on every recomposition.

# Notification catalog assembly correction

Implemented against `aa30d5b` and committed as `6393833`. The implementer ran no builds. Parent verification passed compilation, tests, APK assembly and two mutation probes as recorded below. Follow-up profiling confirmed all four assembly calls on background threads and none on Main; wall duration and startup limitations are recorded below. `git diff --check` passes.

The supplied Perfetto capture measured two `farhan.catalog.assemble` calls on Main totaling 58.128 ms, with a 37.911 ms maximum. The previous final refresh assembled on Main to avoid overwriting edits made during discovery. `RefreshAppPriorityCatalog` now runs both bulk loads and package-index construction on `Dispatchers.Default`, performs discovery on `Dispatchers.IO`, and reconciles edited packages before publishing on the caller/UI context. The existing trace surrounds both bulk loads. `GetAppPriorityInfoList.discover()` scans and updates notification availability without creating a discar

The initial cached publication precedes discovery even if an edit arrives during its assembly. Both the VM's existing refresh job and the refresh owner's in-flight guard suppress overlap. Each edit still immediately refreshes its package through `forPackage()`. The owner records a set of distinct edited package names, bounded by packages touched during this refresh, rather than a queue of edit events. It performs no retries and starts no jobs.

Before each publication, the owner reads current preferences for only those edited packages. It replaces their rows in the background-prepared catalog and retains every other row. These reads and publication have no suspension between them on the serial caller/UI context. Therefore an older background snapshot cannot restore priority, lock, channel, queue order, or rank values after a completed UI edit. Repeated edits to one package cause one reconciliation read using its latest stored values. The refreshed source registry supplies discovered metadata even for edited rows. An edit to a package

Legacy exception rows can appear in `cached()` without a registered source. `forPackage()` now synthesizes the same source for those rows, so reconciliation can refresh their preferences instead of retaining a stale background value. A direct-loader regression test covers this path without a catalog copy or discovery.

Queue preference writes retain the existing IO write followed by a Main row patch. The row patch is the edit's UI completion point and records its package before reading the row. If that completion happens after publication, its direct patch supplies the final value.

The comparator uses notification availability and lowercase app name. Preference edits do not change those sort keys. Discovery updates source names before the final background sort. Reconciliation therefore preserves positions. Arbitrary source metadata updates from other components after an assembly snapshot are outside this refresh's snapshot boundary; the next refresh incorporates their ordering. This change adds no new freshness guarantee for those external updates.

`withContext` checks cancellation on return to the caller, followed by an explicit `ensureActive()` before publication. UI-driven cancellation cannot interleave with the non-suspending reconciliation/publication block. Cancellation remains cooperative if initiated from another thread after the last check. Loader/discovery failures propagate and release the guard; error UI behavior is unchanged.

The VM publishes SnapshotStateList changes on Main and assigns the already prepared package index. It no longer constructs a duplicate package index on Main. Updating the SnapshotStateList remains linear in row count and is separate from classification/sorting/assembly.

## Changed files

- `notification_filter/notification_filter_domain/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/notification_filter_domain/use_cases/RefreshAppPriorityCatalog.kt`: production refresh owner, narrow loader/discovery/package callbacks, injected dispatchers, and prepared rows/index publication.
- `notification_filter/notification_filter_domain/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/notification_filter_domain/use_cases/GetAppPriorityInfoList.kt`: separate discovery API; existing `invoke()` retains discover-then-load behavior; direct row refresh also supports synthesized exception sources.
- `notification_filter/notification_filter_presentation/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/notification_filter_presentation/apppriority/AppPriorityViewModel.kt`: wire the refresh owner, record edited packages, reuse the prepared index.
- `notification_filter/notification_filter_domain/src/test/java/ly/com/tahaben/notification_filter_domain/use_cases/RefreshAppPriorityCatalogTest.kt`: three focused coroutine tests.
- `notification_filter/notification_filter_domain/src/test/java/ly/com/tahaben/notification_filter_domain/use_cases/GetAppPriorityInfoListTest.kt`: discovery-only and synthesized-exception regression tests, plus updated coverage note. Existing assertions are unchanged.
- `research/notification-catalog-perf-report.md`: this handoff.

No provider, dependency, Hilt, schema, or migration changes are needed. `KnownPackageSourceStore.kt` was inspected and left unchanged. Parent-owned ScheduleEditorScreen, test-messenger, and unrelated documentation changes were not edited.

## Focused proofs

All new tests state WHY/CLAIM and a plausible wrong implementation they catch. The refresh tests use the real `GetAppPriorityInfoList.cached()`/`forPackage()` and real classifier with fake preferences/registry/platform services. The discovery callback controls source changes; the separate loader test exercises the real discovery scanners. The production VM invokes this same owner. No Robolectric or duplicated refresh algorithm is used.

- Cached publication precedes discovery; distinct marked coroutine dispatchers identify actual synchronous bulk reads and publisher calls. A paused discovery also allows a second refresh call to prove overlap suppression. Exact prepared index fixtures cover both publications.
- Actual cached and final loader snapshots pause behind deferred gates. Edits during the first assembly, discovery, and final assembly must retain the latest priority, lock, channel offset, order, and rank, as well as discovered rows and changed metadata. Exact per-package read counts prove repeated edits are deduplicated and bulk reads remain two.
- Cancellation while either assembly is held in a non-cancellable block must prevent its later publication. A subsequent refresh must publish twice, proving guard cleanup. No sleeps or wall-clock deadlines are used.
- Real discovery must scan without preference reads used for bulk classification; a subsequent cached load is the positive control for those probes.
- A synthesized exception row must refresh directly to a changed preference even when no registry source exists, with no additional whole-registry read or scan.

- A synthesized exception row must refresh directly to a changed preference even when no registry source exists, with no additional whole-registry read or scan.

content.thinking:
The install is a debug build, and debug Compose with no R8 or baseline profile is likely a big source of the lag. Debuggable apps also run slower, so I'm checking whether the profile compilation step gets skipped on install for this build.

I'm planning the inbox list design now: a presentation model with headers, single rows, and grouped threads, where consecutive notifications from the same app and title get collapsed together.

I'm deciding whether to group by category: I'll check the NotificationCategory enum to see if COMMUNICATION is reliable for messaging apps like Signal, since grouping by package and title alone would wrongly merge things like repeated bank alerts. I also need to group by package, title and section, and the grouped thread should sit at the position of its newest member rather than requiring consecutive items. Open question: where the expanded state of each thread should live.

I'm adding a per-thread expanded state, and I'm planning to hoist it into the ViewModel so the toggle survives recomposition. A collapsed thread will show the newest message with a count and a chevron, and expanding it reveals each message. Swiping the thread dismisses every message in it, tapping the header opens the newest notification, and tapping a nested message opens that one. I'm also considering clamping long single-notification text to three lines, though tapping would still just open the app.

I'm sketching the app icon component next: a 40dp rounded icon loaded off the main thread through PackageManager and cached in an LRU, with a letter placeholder in a tinted circle so the row doesn't shift when the real icon arrives.

I'm checking whether `Drawable.toBitmap` is available, since that would need core-ktx in core-ui. Compose usually pulls in androidx.core anyway, but I'd rather draw the bitmap manually with Bitmap and Canvas to avoid the dependency. I also need to confirm the manifest has what package visibility requires for resolving other apps' icons, since the installed-apps list already works, so it's probably fine.

I'm laying out the delivery states for each row: a "Sent" badge with a check, "Waiting" with a clock, and "Not sent" with a warning when the delivery was invalidated. Sticky section headers will carry counts, and unsent cards get a 1dp outline so they stand apart from the sent ones, which keep the muted container.

I'm settling on how the action buttons should look: swapping the small outlined buttons for filled tonal ones, and dropping the per-item horizontal scroll state.

I'm settling on how the action buttons should look: tonal pill buttons around 40dp tall, sitting in a wrapping row with 8dp spacing, and I'm checking that the touch targets still meet the 48dp minimum.

I'm settling on the button styling now: filled tonal buttons about 40dp tall with generous horizontal padding and label text, relying on the default minimum touch target to keep them at 48dp. I'm also weighing whether to drop the channel chip to cut clutter, but leaning toward keeping it since it's existing information.

I'm settling on a perf plan for the inbox: building the entries list off the main thread, with date labels and grouping done in the ViewModel. I'm weighing whether strong skipping makes an immutable list wrapper unnecessary, since unstable parameters would then be compared by identity.

I'm making the cached rows stable so an unchanged entry that gets rebuilt on each database emission can skip recomposition, since each row is compared by value rather than identity. The row callbacks will also be passed as stable references, so they don't force the item to recompose either.

I'm moving the item callbacks up to the screen as shared lambdas that take the row, so each item doesn't recreate them and recompose on every change. I'm also planning to drop the per-item remembered saveable state, the size tracking, and the per-item dropdown menus in favor of one shared context menu.

I'm thinking about the long-press menu next: the dropdown only needs to exist while it's open, so I'll compose it conditionally instead of keeping one per item. Positioning it near the press point without measuring the item's height is the tricky part, so I'm considering anchoring it to a zero-size box placed at the touch location.

I'm working out how to position the long-press menu: the Box gets absoluteOffset at the press coordinates so it doesn't flip in RTL, and the DropdownMenu anchors to it, which removes the need for onSizeChanged.

I'm weighing the long-press menu positioning: the DropdownMenu would extend leftward from a zero-size anchor in RTL, which is fine since the anchor has no width. The tricky part is that `combinedClickable` doesn't expose the press coordinates, so I'm looking at a `pointerInput` with `detectTapGestures` instead to keep the touch position.

I'm settling the date labels: the ViewModel will compute them on the default dispatcher once per emission, reusing a single formatter and precomputed day boundaries. object NotificationInboxFilter {

    fun effectivePriority(
        item: NotificationItem,
        standingThresholdHours: Int,
        nowMillis: Long = System.currentTimeMillis(),
    ): NotificationPriority {
        val standingCutoffMillis = standingThresholdHours * 3_600_000L
        val isStanding = !item.isRead
            && item.priority != NotificationPriority.CRITICAL
            && (nowMillis - item.timestamp) > standingCutoffMillis
        return if (isStanding) item.priority.degraded(1) else item.priority
    }

    fun filter(
        notifications: List<NotificationItem>,
        priorityFilter: NotificationPriority?,
        standingThresholdHours: Int,
        nowMillis: Long = System.currentTimeMillis(),
    ): List<NotificationItem> {
        if (priorityFilter == null) return notifications
        return notifications.filter { item ->
            effectivePriority(item, standingThresholdHours, nowMillis) == priorityFilter
        }
    }
}

Base directory for this skill: /home/mini/.claude/skills/boat

# Boat

Boat (boat.dev) rents full Linux VMs ("sandboxes"): x86_64 Ubuntu, user
`user`, home `/home/user`, passwordless `sudo`, Docker and common toolchains,
billed per second while running. Older docs and third-party skills call it
**Box** (`box` CLI, `box.ascii.dev`, `on.ascii.dev`): same product, stale
names. Use `boat`. Inside a sandbox, agents get Boat's own `boat` skill; this
one is for driving sandboxes from here.

## Access

- The CLI is `boat` (on `PATH`; `~/.ascii/bin/boat`) and is already signed in:
  `boat status`. Never run `boat login`, `boat onboard` or an install script;
  if it says signed out, ask the user.
- A sandbox is reachable **only through the CLI** (`exec`, `ssh`, `scp`,
  `forward`). It is not on Tailscale and has no entry in `~/.ssh/config`.
- Always pass the explicit `bx_...` id. `current` and `self` do not work from
  a non-interactive shell here.
- Which sandbox: read `<project>.research/boat.md` (id, purpose, size, what
  secrets it holds). Update it when you create, trim or retire one.

## Commands

| Need | Command |
|---|---|
| State, size, TTL | `boat info <id>` (JSON; fields under `.sandbox`), `boat list` |
| Start / stop | `boat resume <id>`, `boat stop <id>` |
| Short command | `boat exec <id> --timeout 120 -- bash -lc '<cmd>'` (default timeout 30 s) |
| Long job | `boat exec <id> --detach -- bash -lc '<cmd> > ~/job.log 2>&1'` → prints `pid` |
| Wait for it | `boat exec <id> --attach <pid>` as a background Bash command (the harness notifies you); `--status <pid>`, `--kill <pid>` |
| Files | `boat scp ./f <id>:/home/user/f`, `boat scp <id>:/home/user/f ./f` |
| Source | `git bundle create x.bundle <branch>`, `scp` it, `git clone x.bundle` inside: no Git credentials enter the sandbox |
| Plan and hours | `boat limits`, `boat usage <id>`; never quote prices from memory |

`exec` prints one JSON line (`stdout`, `stderr`, exit code). Parse it, for
example `| python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.loads(sys.stdin.readline()); print(d["stdout"])'`.

## Gotchas seen here

- **Nix socket after resume.** The first Nix call after `resume` fails with
  "Permission denied" on the daemon socket. A plain restart can leave the
  socket at mode 0644, and a `chmod 666` alone later gives "Connection refused"
  once a detached job starts. What works (one `exec`): `sudo systemctl stop
  nix-daemon.service nix-daemon.socket; sudo rm -f
  /nix/var/nix/daemon-socket/socket; sudo systemctl start nix-daemon.socket
  nix-daemon.service; sleep 3; sudo chmod 666
  /nix/var/nix/daemon-socket/socket; nix store ping`. Then run detached jobs
  under `setpriv` (below). Source
  `/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/etc/profile.d/nix-daemon.sh` in each `exec`.
- **Capabilities.** `exec` processes carry ambient capabilities that break
  FHS/bubblewrap tools. Wrap detached runs:
  `--detach -- setpriv --ambient-caps -all --inh-caps -all bash -lc '...'`.
- **Nothing survives a stop** except the disk: relaunch services after
  `resume`. The IP changes on each resume.
- **Size.** Boat counts allocated disk; a sandbox past the default limit needs
  `--type large` to resume (2× cost). Trim or `nix-store --gc` instead of
  upsizing, and ask before choosing a paid size.
- **Memory.** Sandboxes have their own RAM (the qex queue is for this host),
  but default size is ~8 GB: one Gradle or emulator job at a time.

## Rules

- **Secrets stay put.** Never copy keys, tokens or signing keystores into a
  sandbox, and never print them, unless the user said so for that sandbox.
  `holdsCreatorLogins` in `info` shows whether account logins are on it; a
  sandbox made with `--no-env` has none.
- **Costs.** Stop a sandbox when the work is done. Create one only when the
  task needs it. Delete stopped sandboxes you created once nothing needs them,
  so they don't pile up. Sandboxes owned by another project or session are
  theirs: check (`boat exec <id> -- ps`) before touching one, and never stop
  one that is busy.

## Disk, starts and credit (owner, 2026-11-18)

- **40 GB cap.** When a sandbox's used disk passes 40 GB, start a fresh one
  from a small saved snapshot and stop the old one. Never save a snapshot over
  40 GB: a 49 GB saved snapshot stopped hydrating (stuck in phase `sysdelta`,
  even `echo` timed out), while a 3 GB one was ready in ~10 s. Keep saved
  snapshots to what runs need: toolchains and package caches, not build
  output, run directories or checkouts.
- **Starts.** New sandboxes use the daily start budget (`boat billing status`:
  `limits.starts.day`). While under 50% of it is used, start fresh sandboxes
  freely and don't spend effort cleaning inside them. From 50% on, reuse your
  sandboxes and clean inside them after each run (old run directories,
  finished build output, temp databases, logs already downloaded), harder past
  ~25 GB used. Always keep at least 50 starts in reserve for the day; reuse or
  wait rather than go below it.
- **Credit after the plan runs out.** When the plan's included hours are used
  up, starts draw from the prepaid pack or wallet: check `creditBalanceHours`
  and `canStart` in `boat billing status` before calling Boat empty. Plan-hours
  counters alone undercount.
- **Sign-in.** `boat login` starts a new browser sign-in and signs the CLI out
  until it completes. Never run it from an agent; ask the user.

## Spend: cheap by default, fast under a deadline

Plan hours are finite (`boat limits`: `planIncluded.vmHoursRemaining`), a
`large` sandbox bills 2x, and a keepalive bills while nothing runs. Pick the
mode from the situation and say which one you are in.

| | Cheap (default) | Time crunch (owner deadline) |
|---|---|---|
| When | No deadline given | The owner asked for a result by a time |
| Size | `default` for test iterations; `large` only for full suites, APK builds and jobs that need its RAM | `large` throughout |
| Idle | Sandbox stops itself ~15 min after the last job (`boat-run` and `boat-sync-test` set the idle TTL); stop it explicitly at the end of a batch | Keep it up for the window; still stop it when the deadline work is delivered |
| Runs | Targeted files; batch checks into one run; full suite only at a gate (before pushing a shared branch) | Same targeting; run independent jobs in parallel; start a warm build early |
| Never | Leave a sandbox up overnight, or a 2-hour keepalive for one quick run | Run past the deadline work at `large` "while you are there" |

Check the spend once a session (`boat limits`, `boat usage <id>`) and say it
when the remaining hours will not reach the plan's period end at the current
rate. Shrinking (`boat resume <id> --type default`) needs the data to fit:
trim old run directories and `nix-store --gc` first.
- **Docs.** `https://docs.boat.dev/llms.txt` lists every page; fetch any page
  as `.md`. `boat <command> --help` is authoritative for flags.

content.text:
I changed the Inbox to separate sent from unsent, show app icons and styled buttons, and fold group chats into expandable cards. It compiles and the 9 new logic tests pass, but I never ran it on a device, so I can't say yet whether scrolling feels better or how the new rows look on screen. Nothing is committed.

- **Sent vs unsent:** the Inbox now has three sticky sections: Waiting to send, Not sent and Sent. Not sent covers items Farhan couldn't proxy. Waiting and not-sent cards are outlined and Sent cards are filled. Each card also has a Sent, Waiting or Not sent chip.
- **Icons, buttons, group chats:**
  - Each row shows the app's launcher icon in a fixed box that keeps its size while the icon loads. A new `AppIcon` helper in core-ui loads the icons off the main thread and caches them.
  - The source app's buttons (Reply and so on) are now rounded pill buttons that wrap onto extra lines instead of scrolling sideways.
  - Two or more messages from the same chat (same app and title, communication category) fold into one card. It shows the latest message and a "6 messages · 2 unread" count, and expands to the full list. Swiping the card clears the whole chat.
- **Scroll lag:** Inbox only. The Dashboard and Apps lists are untouched.
  - **Main-thread work:** per-row work now runs off the main thread, including grouping, date labels (rebuilt per row on every redraw before) and the button lookup. That lookup was an O(n) scan per row.
  - **Per-row overhead:** each row used to create a coroutine scope, three saved-state values, a size-measuring callback and a popup menu even at rest. The red swipe background is now only drawn while you swipe.
  - **Skipped redraws:** rows get one shared set of callbacks, so unchanged rows are skipped when the list updates.
  - **Empty state:** the list no longer flashes "No notifications" before the first load.

If the Inbox still lags, the install target is probably the cause: `make install` builds debug, which has no minification and no baseline profile and scrolls Compose lists noticeably worse. Compare against a release-like build before chasing more code. I can add icons or the same fixes to the other lists if you want.

Two things to check on the phone: that icons actually appear (the app already holds the permission to see other apps), and the new chips and wording on real notifications. I didn't make a mock-up for this, since you asked for changes to the running app.

I used the Boat sandbox `bx_bngcafgz` at large size for the build because this host can't build the app. It's stopped now, and `research/boat.md` has the note.

content.thinking:
I'm going to port the work onto the integration branch, starting with a short status note for the user and then making changes with minimal breakage. I'll copy over my new files, checking whether the integration branch's versions of the component files differ, and reuse the existing internal `PackageAppIcon` from the apppriority package.

I'm weighing whether to reuse the existing `PackageAppIcon` or keep my own icon component. I'm considering adding a synchronous cache lookup to the loader so the icon doesn't flicker while scrolling, and then using that in the Inbox as well.

I'm looking at how the icon loader is created: calling it per row would give each row its own cache, so it has to be hoisted to the screen level and passed down. I'll also need to check whether `NotificationListItem` is used anywhere else before making the composables `internal`, since the loader type is internal and would otherwise fail to compile in a public class.

I'm planning the ViewModel next: sections will be computed from the page for both cleared and uncleared items, with `sections` and `expandedThreads` added to the state while the existing fields stay. I'm also weighing whether to move the section preparation off the main thread with `flowOn` on the IO dispatcher, since `getNotificationActionTitles` currently runs in `onEach`, and I need to confirm the test passes in a test dispatcher.

I'm moving the section preparation onto the IO dispatcher with `flowOn`, so the `onEach` that assembles state stays light. The cleared view keeps its empty actions, and I'm planning to add thread dismiss and toggle handlers alongside the existing notification dismissal.

I'm deciding to put the screen-level delay in a single coroutine scope instead of adding a thread-dismiss event, so existing immediate-deletion tests on notification dismissal stay valid. The swipe-to-clear action will queue each item's dismissal after a short pause.

I'm checking how the loading spinner and the Clear button are wired on the integration screen, so I can rewrite the list section to match.
I'm rebuilding the Inbox change on the owner-build branch, since the phone runs that build and its Inbox code differs from mine; I'll reuse its app-icon loader and keep the tests green.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Turn 1: In the running Farhan Android app Inbox: (a) delineate sent from unsent notifications; (b) fix laggy scrolling in notification lists ("all but the settings and homepage"); (c) include app icons and other notification state (well-styled buttons, expanded state e.g. group chats).
   - Turn 2: Icons not rendering; report how many Boat launches (sandbox starts) remain; if some, keep them running or work with another agent on a sandbox still up; don't spend unnecessarily; build a profilable build and Taildrop it ("tail drop me it"). Mid-turn: update instructions to conserve sandbox launches slightly longer when below 20 launches (balanced against burning hours), and don't conserve large boxes due to cost.
   - Turn 3 (latest): ".profileable? No, leave it on the same APK name. Build it on top of the other pilot work please. This APK is unsuitable and installs alongside rather than atop my existing install. That's wrong." ⇒ same applicationId `ly.com.tahaben.farhan_alpha`, built on integration/owner-build (the phone's "owner build D"), installing over the existing install.
   - Standing constraints (user's global CLAUDE.md): Taildrop only to `pixel-9a` (never `google-pixel-9a-work`); commit/push only on request; no upstream outreach; skills edited in mstack not installed dirs; mock-ups owned by orchestrator and shown via html_preview; clock times Mountain (UTC); boat skill: never run `boat login`, always use explicit `bx_…` id, no secrets in sandboxes, stop sandboxes when done except per new <20-starts rule.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Jetpack Compose (BOM 2025.02.00, foundation 1.7.8, Kotlin 2.1.10, strong skipping), LazyColumn + `stickyHeader` (LazyListScope member, no import), `animateItem`, SwipeToDismissBox (LTR workaround), `FlowRow` (ExperimentalLayoutApi), `drawBehind` rail (fillMaxHeight in list Row measures 0), `@Immutable` models, one stable `InboxActions` callback object for skippable rows.
   - Delivery model: `NotificationItem.isDelivered` / `deliveryInvalidated` ⇒ DeliveryState SENT / NOT_SENT / WAITING; sections ordered WAITING, NOT_SENT, SENT; threads = same package + trimmed title + category COMMUNICATION, ≥2 messages, per section.
   - Perf: per-row work moved off Main (`flowOn`), single Calendar/DateFormat per refresh (`NotificationDateLabeler`), `NotificationActionStore.get` is synchronized O(n) prune, icon sync-cache peek to avoid letter-tile flash, debug builds scroll worse than release (no R8/baseline profile).
   - Boat: x86_64 sandboxes, `boat-run` delta sync, large size 2× billing, daily start budget (200/day; 195 used; 4 left after resume), credit pack 1692.05 h, nix socket/stale build dir gotchas; host aarch64 cannot build.
   - Build types: `profileable` (release code, debug-signed, `isDebuggable=false`, manifest `<profileable android:shell="true"/>`), same applicationId so it upgrades the debug install iff signing key matches (Boat debug key) and versionCode (11) not lower.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **Worktree `/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan.worktrees/inbox-sent-unsent` (branch `pilot/inbox-sent-unsent`, from integration/owner-build cbc5fd5; all changes uncommitted)** — the deliverable tree. Base path `notification_filter/notification_filter_presentation/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/notification_filter_presentation/`:
     - `inbox/InboxEntries.kt` (new): `DeliveryState{WAITING("Waiting to send","Waiting"), NOT_SENT("Not sent","Not sent"), SENT("Sent","Sent")}` with `of(item)` (isDelivered→SENT, deliveryInvalidated→NOT_SENT, else WAITING); `InboxMessage(item, displayPriority, delivery, dateTimeLabel, compactLabel, actions)`; `InboxEntry` sealed (`key`, `contentType`); `InboxSection(delivery, entries)` with `key="header:NAME"`, `messageCount`; `InboxSingle`; `InboxThread(key, delivery, messages)` (`latest`, `unreadCount`); `InboxEntryBuilder.build(notifications, displayPriority, actionTitles, labeler): List<InboxSection>`.
     - `components/NotificationListItem.kt` (rewritten, composables `internal`): `InboxActions(iconLoader, onOpen, onAction, onAlwaysAllow, onAppInfo, onToggleThread)`, `NotificationRowCard`, `NotificationThreadCard` (expand, max 30 messages, "N older messages"), `InboxSectionHeader`, `CardFrame` (priority rail via drawBehind, outline border for unsent, PackageAppIcon, long-press menu composed only when open via zero-size absoluteOffset Box), pills for delivery/priority/category/count/channel, `FilledTonalButton` CircleShape action buttons in FlowRow, `priorityColor`, `deliveryIcon`, `deliveryColor`.
     - `components/SwipeToClearBox.kt` (new): background composed only while `dismissDirection != Settled`.
     - `components/NotificationDateLabel.kt`: appended `NotificationDateLabeler(nowMillis, locale)` with `time/date/dateTime/compact`.
     - `apppriority/AppIconLoader.kt`: added `fun peek(packageName, pixels)`; `apppriority/PackageAppIcon.kt`: initial state `loader.peek(...) ?: AppIcon.LetterTile`, load only `if (icon !is AppIcon.Loaded)`.
     - `NotificationFilterState.kt`: added `sections: List<InboxSection> = emptyList()`, `expandedThreads: Set<String> = emptySet()`. `NotificationFilterEvent.kt`: added `OnToggleThread(threadKey)`. `NotificationFilterViewModel.kt`: `.map { prepare(rows, selection) }.flowOn(ioDispatcher).onEach{…}`, `PreparedPage`, `prepare()`, sections reset on page-key change, `OnToggleThread` handler (imports flowOn, map, NotificationDateLabeler, InboxEntryBuilder, InboxSection).
     - `NotificationFilterScreen.kt`: LazyColumn body replaced (sections → `stickyHeader` + `items` with `SwipeToClearBox`/cards, `animateItem(fadeInSpec=null, fadeOutSpec=null, placementSpec=tween(200))`); added `iconLoader = rememberAppIconLoader()`, `clearScope`, `inboxActions`, `onClearItems` (delay(100) then `OnDismissNotification`); kept owner-build `dispatchClear`/`clearLabel` Clear button and `isLoading` gating; removed unused imports.

The suffix variant is now superseded/unwanted.

    val page: Int = 0,

)

The visibility below assumes a user-enabled listener, a notification Android makes visible to Farhan's user/profile and a code actually present in the extras Farhan reads. Custom layout text, missing text, app-group summaries, work-profile policy and private space can independently limit that input. Farhan reads posted title and text today. Its settings cannot grant Android trust. `F-data/service/NotificationService.kt:239–255`. [NotificationListenerService reference](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/service/notification/NotificationListenerService)

| Version | READ AOSP listener behavior |
| --- | --- |
| **Android 14 (API 34)** | Ordinary enabled listener receives the visible posted notification copy, including the code if the publisher puts it in the delivered title/text. The checked AOSP tag has sensitive-content metadata, but its posted and active/snoozed listener paths lack the Android 15 trust/redaction branch. Publisher behavior and profile filtering still apply. `frameworks/base/services/core/java/com/android/server/notification/NotificationManagerService.java:4862–4940,11371–11422,11658–11666`, `core/java/android/service/notification/NotificationListenerService.java:1950–1961`. [Android 14 AOSP notification manager](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/tags/android-14.0.0_r1/services/core/java/com/android/server/notification/NotificationManagerService.java) |
| **Android 15 (API 35)** | With the platform redaction flag active, when the record is marked sensitive and Farhan's UID is untrusted, posted callbacks and active/snoozed list queries return a redacted copy. Farhan's title becomes an app label and its text a replacement string. Action labels and MessagingStyle bodies are also rewritten, with a separate flag for BigText. Visible unmarked records, trusted recipients and builds with the redaction flag off take the ordinary content path. An assistant can mark a record through `Adjustment.KEY_SENSITIVE_CONTENT`. Trust checks cover the signature/role `RECEIVE_SENSITIVE_NOTIFICATIONS` permission, platform signing, a permitted app op or an eligible companion association for the same package and user. Ordinary notification access and unlocking the screen do not supply that trust. `NotificationManagerService.java:5341–5354,6612–6616,11872–11902,11967–12082`, `core/res/AndroidManifest.xml:8303–8312`. [Android 15 behavior changes, OTP redaction](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/15/behavior-changes-all#otp-redaction), [Android 15 AOSP notification manager](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/tags/android-15.0.0_r1/services/core/java/com/android/server/notification/NotificationManagerService.java) |
| **Android 16 (API 36)** | Same default for ordinary listeners when masking is enabled. In the inspected release, QPR1 and QPR2 source, the posted-callback branch also consults the hidden global `REDACT_OTP_NOTIFICATIONS_FROM_UNTRUSTED_LISTENERS` setting, default true. If platform configuration disables that check for callbacks, a visible posted record can be delivered intact. The inspected active/snoozed query helper still uses sensitive-content and trust checks without consulting that override. The setting is hidden platform configuration. `NotificationManagerService.java:2390–2418,2465–2468,6030–6041,13490–13519,13599–13638`, `core/java/android/provider/Settings.java:19825–19831` at `android-16.0.0_r1`. [Android 16 AOSP notification manager](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/tags/android-16.0.0_r1/services/core/java/com/android/server/notification/NotificationManagerService.java), [Android 16 QPR1](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/heads/android16-qpr1-release/services/core/java/com/android/server/notification/NotificationManagerService.java), [Android 16 QPR2](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/heads/android16-qpr2-release/services/core/java/com/android/server/notification/NotificationManagerService.java) |

**READ.** `Ranking.hasSensitiveContent()` is marked `@hide @SystemApi` in the release tags. Farhan's ordinary SDK listener cannot rely on it as a redaction indicator. The Android 15 documentation's `View.setContentSensitivity` and **Disable screen share protections** refer to screen sharing. Settings' **Sensitive notifications** lock-screen preference writes `LOCK_SCREEN_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NOTIFICATIONS`. These controls do not grant unredacted listener access in the inspected source. The checked Android 16 Settings controller for **Enhanced notifications** enables or disables the default notification assistant. **INFERRED.** If that assistant supplies the sensitive marking, disabling it can affect marking on a particular build, with device-wide effects. **UNVERIFIED.** The exact result of that toggle, the platform flag state and any vendor-specific per-app control on the owner's devices. Do not make changing system privacy settings a prerequisite. `frameworks/base/core/java/android/service/notification/NotificationListenerService.java:1962–1971` (API 35), `:2020–2029` (API 36). [Android 15 screen-share and OTP behavior](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/15/behavior-changes-all), [Enhanced notifications controller](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/packages/apps/Settings/+/refs/tags/android-16.0.0_r1/src/com/android/settings/notification/NotificationAssistantPrefer

**INFERRED.** On current Android, Farhan with ordinary notification access cannot reliably read a system-redacted OTP. The paths below have different prerequisites.

- **User toggles.** Notification access enables delivery to the listener. Farhan's package/category/channel selection controls its own processing. A lock-screen display change leaves listener trust unchanged. A build may let the user disable its notification assistant globally, with the limitations above. The Android 16 hidden setting in AOSP is platform configuration, outside the normal Farhan settings contract.
- **Companion association.** A genuine, user-authorized device pairing that qualifies under the platform trust check can preserve access, alongside notification listener authorization. It only fits an actual companion product. **UNVERIFIED.** Behavior on the target handset for a specific association. [Companion device pairing](https://developer.android.com/develop/connectivity/bluetooth/companion-device-pairing)
- **Publisher's own copy.** The source app already has the content it generated. Its own copy action or UI remains the natural fallback. A cooperating publisher could offer a deliberate, user-authorized handoff. Farhan has no general access to another app's internal copy. Do not treat a surviving notification token as access to the code.
- **Accessibility.** A separately enabled accessibility service has a different contract for visible UI and receives only data the platform and publisher expose to it. Farhan already declares an accessibility service for its existing feature. Reusing it for authentication text would expand what it reads. Sensitive-view restrictions and publisher layouts leave OTP access uncertain, so keep this outside the pilot. `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:101–113`. [Android accessibility data sensitivity](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/View#setAccessibilityDataSensitive(int))
- **SMS.** ClearSMS receives the SMS itself as the default messaging app through `ROLE_SMS` and `SMS_DELIVER`, with SMS permissions. That is separate from reading another app's notification. Adopting it would mean becoming an eligible SMS handler and taking on that role, or qualifying for a restricted permission exception. SMS Retriever or SMS User Consent covers supported verification flows with the appropriate sender format or explicit user action. `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:11–13,155–163`, `sms/DefaultSmsAppHelper.kt:18–36`, `receiver/SmsReceiver.kt:107–130`. [Default-handler requirements](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/permissions/default-handlers), [Choose an SMS verification API](https://developers.google.com/identity/sms-retriever/choose-an-api)

content.text:
**Where OTP handling is in Farhan:** nowhere in code yet. No Kotlin file reads, masks or copies one-time codes. It exists only as decisions and research:

- On 2026-11-20 you decided OTP ships as opt-in with a disclaimer (`research/build-loop-state-2026-11-20.md`, "Update ~14:10 UTC").
- The design is in `research/notification-display-language.md` (a labelled masked code, never shown in aggregates or previews) and in the "OTP" section of `research/clearsms-filtering-research.md` (parsing, a sensitive-flagged clipboard copy, no auto-copy).
- The only sensitive-flag code is `AutomationSettingsSection.kt:125`, which flags the automation credential when it copies it. That has nothing to do with OTPs.

**When the GrapheneOS Messaging fork marks something sensitive:** never. I cloned `GrapheneOS/platform_packages_apps_Messaging` (head `89a88b3`) and searched it. Its notification code never sets any sensitivity marker, and it never sets a public version of a notification. The only related call is `setVisibility(VISIBILITY_PRIVATE)`, which it applies to every notification it posts. Examples are `BugleNotifications.java:285,590` and `MessageNotificationState.java:889`. That setting only hides content on the lock screen, and it applies to all messages, not just codes.

Any OTP redaction your phone does is therefore done by the system, not by Messaging. As I read the AOSP source in the earlier research, Android 15 and later redact a notification only when it is marked sensitive and the listener is untrusted. The marking comes from the system's notification assistant, which Android does not ship by default. That is probably why your OTP apps show codes unredacted, which matches your earlier note.

**A toggle:** this can't be done in Messaging alone, because there is no public app-side flag. Two options:

1. **Messaging-side setting.** Add a "hide verification codes on lock screen" switch that posts those notifications with a redacted public version. That is a small patch to the fork, but it only changes the lock screen. A listener like Farhan would still see the full text.
2. **Farhan-side.** The plan is already to run OTP detection in Farhan itself, as opt-in. It parses the delivered notification text, shows a masked code, and copies it with the sensitive clip flag. That works without any system marking.

I recommend option 2. Option 1 is worth doing only if you want codes hidden on the lock screen. Tell me which you want.

Sources:
- [GrapheneOS/platform_packages_apps_Messaging](https://github.com/GrapheneOS/platform_packages_apps_Messaging)
- [Android 15 behavior changes, OTP redaction](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/15/behavior-changes-all#otp-redaction)

# Boat

Boat (boat.dev) rents full Linux VMs ("sandboxes"): x86_64 Ubuntu, user
`user`, home `/home/user`, passwordless `sudo`, Docker and common toolchains,
billed per second while running. Older docs and third-party skills call it
**Box** (`box` CLI, `box.ascii.dev`, `on.ascii.dev`): same product, stale
names. Use `boat`. Inside a sandbox, agents get Boat's own `boat` skill; this
one is for driving sandboxes from here.

## Access

- The CLI is `boat` (on `PATH`; `~/.ascii/bin/boat`) and is already signed in:
  `boat status`. Never run `boat login`, `boat onboard` or an install script;
  if it says signed out, ask the user.
- A sandbox is reachable **only through the CLI** (`exec`, `ssh`, `scp`,
  `forward`). It is not on Tailscale and has no entry in `~/.ssh/config`.
- Always pass the explicit `bx_...` id. `current` and `self` do not work from
  a non-interactive shell here.
- Which sandbox: read `<project>.research/boat.md` (id, purpose, size, what
  secrets it holds). Update it when you create, trim or retire one.

## Commands

| Need | Command |
|---|---|
| State, size, TTL | `boat info <id>` (JSON; fields under `.sandbox`), `boat list` |
| Start / stop | `boat resume <id>`, `boat stop <id>` |
| Short command | `boat exec <id> --timeout 120 -- bash -lc '<cmd>'` (default timeout 30 s) |
| Long job | `boat exec <id> --detach -- bash -lc '<cmd> > ~/job.log 2>&1'` → prints `pid` |
| Wait for it | `boat exec <id> --attach <pid>` as a background Bash command (the harness notifies you); `--status <pid>`, `--kill <pid>` |
| Files | `boat scp ./f <id>:/home/user/f`, `boat scp <id>:/home/user/f ./f` |
| Source | `git bundle create x.bundle <branch>`, `scp` it, `git clone x.bundle` inside: no Git credentials enter the sandbox |
| Plan and hours | `boat limits`, `boat usage <id>`; never quote prices from memory |

`exec` prints one JSON line (`stdout`, `stderr`, exit code). Parse it, for
example `| python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.loads(sys.stdin.readline()); print(d["stdout"])'`.

## Gotchas seen here

- **Nix socket after resume.** The first Nix call after `resume` fails with
  "Permission denied" on the daemon socket. A plain restart can leave the
  socket at mode 0644, and a `chmod 666` alone later gives "Connection refused"
  once a detached job starts. What works (one `exec`): `sudo systemctl stop
  nix-daemon.service nix-daemon.socket; sudo rm -f
  /nix/var/nix/daemon-socket/socket; sudo systemctl start nix-daemon.socket
  nix-daemon.service; sleep 3; sudo chmod 666
  /nix/var/nix/daemon-socket/socket; nix store ping`. Then run detached jobs
  under `setpriv` (below). Source
  `/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/etc/profile.d/nix-daemon.sh` in each `exec`.
- **Capabilities.** `exec` processes carry ambient capabilities that break
  FHS/bubblewrap tools. Wrap detached runs:
  `--detach -- setpriv --ambient-caps -all --inh-caps -all bash -lc '...'`.
- **Nothing survives a stop** except the disk: relaunch services after
  `resume`. The IP changes on each resume.
- **Size.** Boat counts allocated disk; a sandbox past the default limit needs
  `--type large` to resume (2× cost). Trim or `nix-store --gc` instead of
  upsizing, and ask before choosing a paid size.
- **Memory.** Sandboxes have their own RAM (the qex queue is for this host),
  but default size is ~8 GB: one Gradle or emulator job at a time.

## Rules

- **Secrets stay put.** Never copy keys, tokens or signing keystores into a
  sandbox, and never print them, unless the user said so for that sandbox.
  `holdsCreatorLogins` in `info` shows whether account logins are on it; a
  sandbox made with `--no-env` has none.
- **Costs.** Stop a sandbox when the work is done. Create one only when the
  task needs it. Delete stopped sandboxes you created once nothing needs them,
  so they don't pile up. Sandboxes owned by another project or session are
  theirs: check (`boat exec <id> -- ps`) before touching one, and never stop
  one that is busy.
