input.message:
Owner follow-up: pairing still fails on the Pixel (Android 17) even after trying the port from BOTH the Wireless debugging main screen and the pairing dialog, and they want much better visibility. Add an in-app diagnostic in the same worktree (/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan.worktrees/inbox-sent-unsent, uncommitted, on top of your pairing rewrite), build a new APK, report summary-first.

1. Connection log: a bounded in-memory ring buffer (last ~200 lines) of FarhanSelfAdb events with UTC and local time, step name, outcome, exception class AND message and the cause chain (class + message), plus the TLS details when available (negotiated protocol, cipher, peer cert subject/algorithm, alert text). Port numbers and host are allowed in this log (ephemeral, not secret). NEVER log the pairing code, the private key, the adb public key bytes, or command output; scrub any run of 6 digits that equals the typed code and any exception message containing it. Keep the existing Log.w lines.
2. A "Connection check" button on the Special access flow page (wireless debugging route) that needs NO pairing code and changes nothing on the phone. It reports, line by line: Android version/SDK and targetSdk; Settings.Global adb_enabled, adb_wifi_enabled; whether Wi-Fi is connected (ConnectivityManager, transport + whether the network is validated) and the phone's own Wi-Fi IPv4; mDNS discovery of _adb-tls-pairing._tcp and _adb-tls-connect._tcp for ~8 s, listing every service found (name, host, port, whether the port is listening on 127.0.0.1 and on the Wi-Fi IP); for the typed port (if any) and each discovered port: TCP connect to 127.0.0.1:port and to the Wi-Fi IP:port with the result and time; then a TLS handshake attempt to each reachable pairing candidate using the same TLS context the pairing uses, reporting protocol, cipher, handshake time or the exact exception (class, message, cause chain), and the result of exportKeyingMaterial. Stop before sending any SPAKE2 message, so it never consumes the pairing code (a pairing attempt may consume it; the check must not).
3. The flow page shows the last result and has "Copy log" (clipboard, sensitive flag like the verification code copy) and "Share log" (ACTION_SEND text/plain) buttons so the owner can paste or send the whole log. Add a short line above the buttons: "Send this to me if pairing fails." Keep styling calm like the rest of the Special access page (no accent fill), copy per writing-copy. Put all strings in core/src/main/res/values/strings.xml.
4. Pairing attempt itself: after a failure, append the full structured trace to the same log, and ALSO try, on a failed TLS handshake only, the alternative the working apps use if different from yours (for example SSLContext from the platform provider vs the standalone Conscrypt, or TLS 1.2 vs 1.3) as a labelled second attempt in the same press; report which variant succeeded or failed, so a single press yields a comparison. Never retry after the code was already sent.
5. Pure logic (log scrubbing, line formatting, ring buffer, check report assembly with fakes) unit tested; keep state in the existing pure presentation layer where possible. Run privileged_access_* tests, :app:testDebugUnitTest and :app:assembleProfileable on Boat as before (sandbox bx_bngcafgz, TTL just extended ~2 h), test the check and the log on the Android 15 emulator and report what it printed (paste a short sample, with ports only). Leave the APK in the sandbox at the same path and give sha256.
Also tell me whether the earlier APK's failure line "Pairing failed at: ..." is shown, in code, for every failure path.

cd /home/mini/Documents/repos/mstack && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='skills/build-loop/references/scoping.md'
s=open(p).read()
anchor="  ledger at every build.\n"
assert s.count(anchor)==1
add=anchor+"""- **Version checklist for every build the owner installs (owner, 2026-11-22).** Version metadata is how the owner,
  a crash log and the ledger agree on which build ran. Before handing over a build:
  1. The build number (Android `versionCode`) is higher than the last build you handed over, every time, and comes
     from a counter in the repo that the build reads, never from memory or a hand edit. Same application id and
     signing key, so it installs over the last one. Never reuse a number for different contents.
  2. The version name keeps the project's base name and adds the short commit and `-dirty` when the tree has
     uncommitted changes, so a crash report header (name and code) points at a commit.
  3. Read the numbers back from the built file (`aapt2 dump badging`: package, versionCode, versionName), not from
     the source, and compare them with the counter.
  4. The file name carries the base, the feature set and the build number.
  5. The delivery message gives package, build number, version name, size and sha256, says "replaces build N", and
     says whether it should install over the current one. Tell the owner to compare the number on their phone.
  6. The ledger entry records number, sha256, base commit, contents and evidence. If a log or screenshot from the
     owner shows a number you did not hand over, or the same number for different contents, fix the counter first.
"""
s=s.replace(anchor,add)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
git diff --stat; git -c user.name="$(git config user.name)" -c user.email="$(git config user.email)" commit -q -am "build-loop: version checklist for every build the owner installs

# Update scout-module locks

Use this skill when a change in a satellite repository needs to be reflected in a
phoe-nix scout module's `flake.lock` files.

Before any push, show the user the change and ask for confirmation to push it to
GitHub. Do not infer push approval from approval to edit files or update locks.

After the user confirms:

1. Commit the satellite repository change with a scoped message, then push the
   intended branch to GitHub.
2. Inspect every relevant `flake.nix` in phoe-nix, including the top-level
   `flake.nix` and affected `scout-modules/*/flake.nix` files. Confirm that each
   usage points to the intended fork, repository, and branch. If any reference is
   wrong or ambiguous, stop and ask before updating locks.
3. From the phoe-nix checkout, update the satellite input and all affected scout
   modules. For example, when updating usagewindow and agent-integration:

   ```sh
   cd ~/Documents/repos/phoe-nix
   nix flake update usagewindow
   nix scout update usagewindow agent-integration
   git add scout-modules/*/flake.lock
   ```

4. Review the staged lockfile diff. Stage only the affected scout-module lock
   files, verify that no unrelated files changed, and report the exact lockfiles
   updated. Do not commit or push phoe-nix unless the user separately asks for
   that.

Do not update a lock from an unpublished local branch, silently retarget a flake
input, or run a broad lock update when named inputs and modules are sufficient.

<summary>Agent "Fix self-ADB pairing failure" finished</summary>
<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>The Pixel pairing failure is still unexplained. This build adds a full connection log, a "Connection check", and a labelled multi-variant pairing attempt. The Android 15 emulator shows pairing and the check work. On the real phone only the owner's logs will say why it fails.

**What the v5 report most likely was**
- **Misattribution:** the v5 "connecting to the port (SocketException)" was probably the retry's failure, not the first attempt's. When the typed port failed, we retried on the mDNS-discovered port and reported only that second failure. The first attempt may have been the one adbd saw and failed, which would match its "Pairing unsuccessful" dialog.
- **Step boundaries:** in v5, connect-socket held only `Socket()` plus options plus `connect`. It never covered TLS, but the first read after the handshake was filed under the SPAKE2 step.
- **Fixes:** the steps are now exact: connect-socket (TCP connect only, options set before connecting), tls-handshake (wrap plus handshake), first-read (new step), export-keying-material, spake2, peer-info. First-read exists because TLS 1.3 shows a refused client certificate only as a reset or alert on the first read. The emulator confirmed this: with no client certificate, the failure appears at first-read as `TLSV1_ALERT_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED`.
- **Reported failure:** if both the typed-port attempt and the discovery retry break before the code is used, the typed port's failure is now the one reported.

**The connection log**
- **Contents:** a ring buffer of the last 200 lines, in memory only. Each line has UTC and local time, operation, step, outcome, and the exception class, message and full cause chain. TLS details (protocol, cipher, socket class, daemon certificate subject/signature/key) are logged after a handshake. The existing `Log.w`/`Log.i` lines under `FarhanSelfAdb` are kept.
- **Scrubbing:** the pairing code is masked while a pairing is in progress. Any exception message containing it is replaced with `<message withheld>`. Base64-like runs of 60 or more characters are withheld. The code, private key, adb public key bytes and command output are never passed in.

**Connection check**
- It sits on the flow page for the wireless route, both beside the form and under a failure. It uses no code, changes nothing, and stops before any SPAKE2 message. It lists:
  - Android and SDK, `targetSdk`, `adb_enabled`/`adb_wifi_enabled`, and `ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK` (declared/granted).
  - Wi-Fi IPv4 and interfaces.
  - Every mDNS pairing and connect service found in 8 s: name, host, port, and whether the port is listening on loopback and on the Wi-Fi IP.
  - A TCP connect to each of the typed port and the discovered ports, on 127.0.0.1 and on the Wi-Fi IP.
  - A TLS probe per way of connecting (see the variants below), each through connect, handshake, first read and key export.
  - A plain adb banner probe on connect ports.
  - A note when the typed port is the connect port.
- **Wi-Fi limit:** ConnectivityManager state (transport, validated) cannot be read. The app deliberately strips `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE` (`tools:node="remove"` in `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`), so the check reads the interface list for the Wi-Fi IP and says connectivity is unreadable. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Owner builds: raise the build number (Android versionCode) by one and print what to pass to Gradle.
#
#   scripts/bump-build.sh          bump gradle/libs.versions.toml, print the number and the build tag
#   scripts/bump-build.sh --show   print them without bumping
#
# Run it once before each build the owner will install, then build with the printed -PbuildTag. Afterwards check
# the APK with scripts/apk-version.sh. Never reuse a number for different contents.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
TOML="$ROOT/gradle/libs.versions.toml"
current="$(sed -n 's/^app-versionCode = "\([0-9]*\)"$/\1/p' "$TOML")"
[ -n "$current" ] || { echo "app-versionCode not found in $TOML" >&2; exit 1; }

if [ "${1:-}" = "--show" ]; then
  number="$current"
else
  number=$((current + 1))
  sed -i "s/^app-versionCode = \"[0-9]*\"$/app-versionCode = \"$number\"/" "$TOML"
fi

tag=""
if git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --short=7 HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  tag="+g$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --short=7 HEAD)"
  [ -z "$(git -C "$ROOT" status --porcelain -- . ':!gradle/libs.versions.toml')" ] || tag="$tag-dirty"
fi
echo "versionCode=$number"
echo "buildTag=$tag"
echo "gradle: -PbuildTag=$tag"
EOF

content.text:
Build 12 is sent to `pixel-9a` by Taildrop. The command exited 0, but I haven't confirmed delivery. The file is `research/apk/farhan-cbc5fd5-connector-b12-profileable.apk`. It should install over your current app, since the package is the same and the build number is higher.

**What I read from the APK itself:**
- **Package:** `ly.com.tahaben.farhan_alpha`.
- **Version code:** 12, and it replaces build 11.
- **Version name:** `0.2.6-alpha+gcfeb20d-dirty`.
- **Size and hash:** 37,290,148 bytes, sha256 `9a4cd6f74f0a53bf993f6c37e84dc3a0c0c295a9af2da761e2f882cd06c108d9`.
- **On your phone:** the About screen shows "version (code)", so it should read `0.2.6-alpha+gcfeb20d-dirty (12)`.

**Not verified:**
- **Pixel (Android 17):** I don't know why pairing failed there, and nothing here was run on it.
- **Emulator (Android 15):** the agent tested the build just before its last small change. The rebuild with the version tag only ran the app unit tests, not the emulator.
- **Last change:** it adds `LinkLost` and the first-failure report. Its unit tests were run, but it was not run on the emulator.
- **Wi-Fi state:** the connection check can't read whether the Wi-Fi network is validated or its transport type, because the app strips the network-state permission on purpose. The agent asks whether you'd allow adding `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE` for that line.

**What changed from build 11:**
- **Exact steps:** the failing step is now exact. Connect, TLS handshake, first read, key export, SPAKE2 and peer info are each separate.
- **Likely cause of your screenshot:** the agent thinks the "connecting to the port (SocketException)" message was the retry's failure, not the first attempt's. The first attempt may have been the one Android's "Pairing unsuccessful" dialog was about.
- **Connection check:** the new button needs no code and changes nothing.
- **Pairing variants:** one press now tries up to five variants:
  - Loopback address `127.0.0.1`.
  - The Wi-Fi IP instead of loopback.
  - No client certificate.
  - The platform TLS provider.
  - The old certificate shape.
  - A variant runs only if the one before it failed before the code was used.
- **Copy and share:** Copy log and Share log buttons are on the flow page.
- **Failure line coverage:** the "Pairing failed at: …" line now shows when a step threw. It does not show when the daemon refused the code or the pairing screen wasn't found.

**What to send me:** try pairing once, then press Connection check, then Copy log (or Share log). The per-variant lines will show which way works.

**Version counter:** it now exists in the worktree. `scripts/bump-build.sh` raises the code in `gradle/libs.versions.toml` and prints the `-PbuildTag=+g<sha>[-dirty]` to pass to Gradle. `scripts/apk-version.sh` reads the package, code, name, size and sha256 from the built file. The next build runs the bump first, so it will be 13. All of this is uncommitted.

The log you pasted points at Android refusing Farhan network access, so the pairing never got as far as TLS or the code. I think it's most likely GrapheneOS's per-app Network permission being off for Farhan. I'm inferring that from the symptoms and haven't confirmed it on your phone.

**What the log shows:**
- **Immediate failure:** every attempt fails at `connect-socket` within a few milliseconds with `socket failed: EPERM (Operation not permitted)`. That error means the phone refused to create a network socket at all.
- **The same fault in the other checks:** the check's plain TCP connect to `127.0.0.1` fails the same way, and Android's network service discovery (NSD) won't even start.
- **Not a protocol problem:** the earlier messages blamed ports and TLS, but the log says nothing about either. The old build only reported the exception class name (`SocketException`), which hid the EPERM message.
- **The permission is declared:** I checked the build 12 file itself, and it declares `INTERNET`. So the phone is denying it despite that.
- **Likely cause:** I believe you run GrapheneOS, which has a per-app Network toggle. An app updated to newly request internet access can start with it off. The "Wi-Fi IPv4 none" line is probably wrong for the same reason.

**What to try now, no new build needed:**
1. Go to App info, then Farhan, then Permissions, then Network. Set it to Allow.
2. Open Settings, then More, then Special access, and try the flow again, with the pairing dialog open in split screen.

If you don't see a Network toggle, or it is already on, tell me. I'd then suspect something like a firewall or an always-on VPN setting, and the log would still say which.

**What I'm doing:** I've asked the agent to detect this case up front and say so plainly, with a button to open Farhan's app settings. The check will run before asking for a code, and it will skip the four variants, since one EPERM means retrying is pointless. The next build, number 13, runs `scripts/bump-build.sh` first and reads its version back from the built file.

**Mistake of mine:** I told you that adding the internet permission was just a copy change. I should have warned that on GrapheneOS it can arrive switched off after an update.

- It reports `Denied` only when the permission is refused or the self-test fails with EPERM. Any other self-test failure, such as a timeout, is logged but is not a denial.
- Its result is logged as `Network permission: denied|granted (checkSelfPermission(INTERNET)=…; loopback self-test …)`.
- A `SocketException` whose own text or cause chain contains `EPERM` or `Operation not permitted` is recognised as a refusal.
- `StepFailure` now has `detail` and `networkDenied`. The message is kept only when it is a refusal.
- Mid-flight EPERM maps to a new `PairingResult.NetworkDenied` and `RouteBlocker.NETWORK_DENIED`, and stops the variants at once.
- On `NsdStartDiscoveryFailed` the preflight is asked again. If the network is off, that is reported as the cause. A lone NSD failure is not treated as a denial, because it can have other causes.
- `NETWORK_DENIED` does not forget the stored key.

**UI**
- When the pairing page opens (and on Try again, or when you pick wireless debugging), Farhan asks whether network access is allowed. If it is denied, the code form is replaced by the message, an "Open Farhan's app settings" button, and the Connection log section. No code is asked for.
- The same message and button show under a failure. A switch toggle that finds the network off opens the flow page with this message instead of a toast.
- The button opens `ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS` for our package.
- The step line shows the real EPERM text only for a refusal, for example "Pairing failed at: connecting to the port (SocketException: socket failed: EPERM (Operation not permitted))".
- The message text is in `core/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`:
  - Message: "Farhan's network access is off. Farhan uses it only to talk to this phone. Turn it on in App info, Permissions, Network (GrapheneOS), or in your phone's app network settings, then try again."
  - Button: "Open Farhan's app settings".

**Connection check**
- The first line is now the network line. If denied, it includes the same hint, then the phone facts follow. After that the network probes are skipped, with a line saying so, because they could only fail.
- A Wi-Fi line with no IPv4 now says "none" can be wrong when Farhan's network access is denied.

**Emulator**
- A real EPERM is not reproducible there. `pm revoke` can't touch INTERNET.
- Instead I used `cmd connectivity set-package-networking-enabled false`. That dropped Farhan's packets, so connects timed out rather than returning EPERM.
- The check printed `Network permission: granted (checkSelfPermission(INTERNET)=GRANTED; loopback self-test failed: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: …)` as its first line and did not call it a denial, as intended. mDNS and TCP then timed out.
- With networking re-enabled it printed `Network permission: granted (…; loopback self-test ok)`.
- The EPERM mapping is covered by unit tests only: message variants, permission denied, a loopback failure that is not EPERM, the variant short-circuit, state mapping, the toggle opening the flow, and the check's first line and skip.

**Not verified on the Pixel**
- That GrapheneOS reports `checkSelfPermission(INTERNET)` as denied when the toggle is off.
- That the loopback self-test gets EPERM there.
- That `NetworkInterface` enumeration works with the toggle off.
- The owner's build-12 log already shows EPERM on both the connect and the loopback TCP, so at least one of the two signals should fire.

**Files**
- Domain: `SelfAdbFailure.kt`, `Routes.kt`, `PrivilegedAccess.kt`.
- Presentation: `SpecialAccessModel.kt`, `PrivilegedAccessViewModel.kt`.
- Selfadb: new `NetworkPreflight.kt`; changes to `AdbPairingClient.kt`, `AndroidSelfAdbRoute.kt`, `ConnectionCheck.kt`, `AndroidCheckProbes.kt`, `AdbDiscovery.kt`.
- App: `SpecialAccessText.kt`, `SpecialAccessFlow.kt`, `SpecialAccessController.kt`, `SettingsScreen.kt`.
- `scripts/bump-build.sh` raised `gradle/libs.versions.toml` to versionCode 13.
- Nothing is committed.
